title: When2Reflect: Predicting Utility of Reflection in Language Models
summary: Can a model's internal representations predict whether self-reflection will improve, harm, or leave unchanged the outcome of a reasoning trajectory?
description: Research project investigating whether internal model representations can predict when self-reflection will improve, harm, or leave unchanged the outcome of an LLM reasoning trajectory.

The framework compares direct reasoning and reflection-induced continuations that start from identical intermediate reasoning states, so the effect of reflection can be measured counterfactually rather than across different problems.
highlights: Developed a counterfactual framework that compares direct reasoning and reflection-induced continuations from identical intermediate reasoning states.
Built an evaluation pipeline over 100 MATH problems, 376 intermediate reasoning states, and 4,512 model rollouts.
Trained hidden-state probes for predicting reflection utility and compared their performance with uncertainty- and confidence-based triggering signals.
Improved reflection-utility prediction from 0.07 to 0.37 Spearman correlation relative to uncertainty-based baselines.
Investigating where reflection utility emerges across transformer layers and how learned signals can support adaptive reflection policies.

metrics.label: Spearman correlation
metrics.context: Reflection-utility prediction: hidden-state probes vs. uncertainty-based baselines (reported in CV).

metrics.label: model rollouts
metrics.context: Across 100 MATH problems and 376 intermediate reasoning states.

title: CLARO: Multi-Agent Deliberation for Civic & Policy Decision-Making
affiliation: UC San Diego · advised by Dr. Nadir Weibel
summary: A multimodal agentic decision-support system for civic policy analysis that decomposes each query into a dependency-aware execution DAG of specialized capabilities.
description: CLARO is a multimodal agentic decision-support system for civic policy analysis. It dynamically decomposes user queries into dependency-aware execution DAGs spanning specialized reasoning, retrieval, analysis, and stakeholder-analysis capabilities.
Completed analytical results stream to the interface as they finish, while conversational synthesis and speech generation proceed asynchronously.
highlights: Architected a planner-driven orchestration layer with 7+ registered capabilities, dynamically activating required agents and tools per query.
Executes independent tasks concurrently with bounded parallelism, dependency scheduling, timeouts, and failure isolation.
Integrated LLM tool use and RAG-based structured evidence retrieval so agents return typed, source-grounded analytical results.
Built contextual data pipelines incorporating location-specific demographic, policy, and spatial information, with dynamic generation of plots from structured outputs.
Designed a progressive WebSocket-based interaction architecture that reduces perceived response latency.
Benchmarked on historical civic-deliberation records, achieving ~75% stakeholder-conflict coverage.

Developing StakeBench and SchemeBench, argument-mining-based frameworks for studying whether multi-agent synthesis disproportionately preserves, amplifies, or suppresses particular stakeholder perspectives.

metrics.label: stakeholder-conflict coverage
metrics.context: Benchmarked on historical civic-deliberation records (reported in CV).

metrics.label: registered capabilities
metrics.context: Activated per query by the planner.

title: Algorithmic Safety Layer for Autonomous LLM Agents
summary: A safety framework that applies Model Predictive Control and convex optimization to keep LLM-driven agents' state transitions within constraints.
description: Designed and implemented a safety framework for LLM-driven autonomous agents, applying Model Predictive Control (MPC) and convex optimization to guarantee safe state transitions during dynamic environment interactions.
highlights: Applied Model Predictive Control and convex optimization to constrain agent state transitions.
Achieved a ~55% reduction in constraint violations over unconstrained baselines without compromising task accomplishment.

title: Resilient Multi-Agent Systems for High-Risk Environments
summary: Hierarchical dynamic-leadership coordination for 15+ agents in simulated wildfire rescue, tested under packet loss and communication lapses.
description: Implemented two hierarchical dynamic-leadership algorithms to improve coordination and fault tolerance in a multi-agent system of 15+ agents operating in simulated wildfire rescue environments.
highlights: Implemented 2 hierarchical dynamic-leadership algorithms for coordination and fault tolerance.
Validated resilience by introducing real-time packet loss and simulated communication lapses, forcing agents to rely on adaptive planning and autonomous task decomposition.
Improved plan adaptation (+15%) and spatial reasoning (+25%) over static coordination baselines under degraded communication.

metrics.label: plan adaptation
metrics.context: Versus static coordination baselines under degraded communication (reported in CV).

title: Hybrid RAG System for Genomics
summary: A two-stage retrieval pipeline for genomic research text: hybrid BM25 + dense search followed by cross-encoder re-ranking.
description: A specialized retrieval-augmented generation pipeline for genomic research data, orchestrating ensemble embedding models and context-aware chunking to capture diverse semantic nuances in biological text.
highlights: Ensemble embedding models with context-aware chunking for biological text.
Two-stage retrieval: hybrid BM25 + dense search, then cross-encoder re-ranking.
~25% improvement in retrieval recall over single-stage dense retrieval on complex biomedical queries.

metrics.label: higher retrieval recall
metrics.context: Versus single-stage dense retrieval on complex biomedical queries (reported in CV).

title: MediPredict: ML-Powered Disease Prediction System
summary: A disease prediction system built on a weighted ensemble of classifiers, with an end-to-end pipeline from preprocessing to an interactive frontend.
description: A disease prediction system using a weighted ensemble of classification models to improve robustness across symptoms.
highlights: Weighted ensemble of classification models for robustness across symptoms.
End-to-end pipeline: preprocessing, model inference, REST APIs, and an interactive frontend for real-time predictions.

title: CovVaxPulse: Sentiment Analysis of the COVID-19 Vaccination Drive
summary: Ingestion and multilingual NLP pipeline tracking temporal trends in public opinion on COVID-19 vaccination from social media.
description: Collected localised vaccination-related data from social media and applied NLP-based sentiment analysis to track temporal trends in public opinion toward COVID-19 vaccination.
highlights: Ingestion pipeline collecting localised vaccination-related posts from X and Reddit, with scheduled jobs and API integrations.
Scalable preprocessing for noisy social media text: language detection, normalization, and multilingual embeddings in a shared semantic space.
Sentiment analysis tracking temporal trends in public opinion.
